sample.packing_or_protection: Multi-layer: outer XOR-decrypting stub -> self-relocating PE loader shellcode -> PECompact2-packed second-stage PE

executive_summary.one_sentence_summary: This sample is a multi-layer packed malware with a loader shellcode that performs in-place process hollowing, but the terminal payload behavior could not be observed locally.
executive_summary.plain_language_assessment: The sample is confirmed malicious through a multi-layer packing scheme. The outermost layer is a PE32 stub that uses XOR decryption to reveal a self-relocating shellcode loader. That shellcode reads its own file, decodes an embedded PECompact2-packed second-stage PE, and rewrites the parent process's memory (process hollowing). The same decryption key is reused across multiple layers, confirming they are part of a single malicious chain. However, the sample never reached its entry point in our analysis environment because two import dependencies (a DisplaySaveSettings function from DESK.cpl and a DispatchMessageA function from USER32) could not be resolved. As a result, the terminal payload behavior — what the PECompact2-packed stage actually does — remains unknown from local evidence. Public sandbox reports describe C2 callback, persistence, and file writes, but these were not locally reproduced.
executive_summary.remaining_decision_point: Terminal payload capability of the PECompact2-packed second stage cannot be determined without further unpacking or a bypass of the loader gate.

confirmed_findings.title: Multi-layer packing confirmed
confirmed_findings.summary: The sample uses three layers: a XOR-decrypting PE32 stub, a self-relocating PE loader shellcode, and a PECompact2-packed second-stage PE. The same key (0x9A246A73) is reused across layers.

confirmed_findings.title: Recovered shellcode performs in-place process hollowing
confirmed_findings.summary: The 1717-byte decrypted shellcode is a self-relocating, two-phase PE loader. Phase A resolves APIs and self-relocates. Phase B reads the parent module file, delta-decodes an embedded PE at file offset 0x50BA, and rewrites the parent's PEB/LDR entry to execute it.

confirmed_findings.title: Loader-phase termination explained
confirmed_findings.summary: The sample terminates during Windows loader initialization with STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND because two import slots cannot be resolved: DispatchMessageA (USER32) is NULL, and DESK.cpl!DisplaySaveSettings is unpatched. This is an environment-gated import dependency, not an intentional anti-debug check.

confirmed_findings.title: Cryptnet imports resolve to real addresses
confirmed_findings.summary: The five cryptnet imports (CryptGetTimeValidObject, etc.) resolve to real cryptnet.dll addresses in the VM. They are not fabricated or garbage exports.

confirmed_findings.title: No anti-analysis measures in the recovered shellcode
confirmed_findings.summary: The recovered shellcode contains no rdtsc, GetTickCount, IsDebuggerPresent, or other anti-debug/anti-VM logic.

confirmed_findings.title: 50-deep wrapper call chain is pure obfuscation
confirmed_findings.summary: The parent stub's 50-deep linear chain of wrapper functions serves only to delay and confuse analysis. The real decryptor is at the end of the chain.

confirmed_findings.title: Second-stage PE is PECompact2-packed (BitSum Technologies)
confirmed_findings.summary: The decoded second-stage PE is packed with PECompact2 (BitSum Technologies), confirmed by local markers and VirusTotal. Its terminal capability is not statically visible.

findings_with_caveats.title: Decryptor destination address unknown but content-independent
findings_with_caveats.summary: The shellcode decryptor's write destination (from LoadLibraryW return + 0x11C) is unknown because the process terminates before reaching the decryptor. However, the decrypted content was recovered independently of the destination address.
findings_with_caveats.caveat: The destination matters for full runtime memory layout reconstruction but does not affect the recovered shellcode logic.

findings_with_caveats.title: msvcrt!fwprintf detour hook present but unconfirmed at runtime
findings_with_caveats.summary: The shellcode builds a detour hook on msvcrt!fwprintf using a push/ret trampoline, gated by a config slot. The hook's enable state and redirect target are not runtime-confirmed.
findings_with_caveats.caveat: The hook may be a data-gathering or anti-forensics mechanism, but its purpose and enable state are inferred from static analysis only.

findings_with_caveats.title: Bypass attempts blocked by loader commit timing
findings_with_caveats.summary: Three bypass approaches (NtTerminateProcess stub redirect, import-descriptor zeroing, IAT patching) were attempted but all executed too late relative to the loader's abort decision.
findings_with_caveats.caveat: A loader-level patch point (e.g., LdrpInitializeProcess hook) was not pursued. The ntdll code pages are PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, preventing in-place patching.

not_supported_claims.claim: The sample is a 'fake AV' or 'fkealrt' family member.
not_supported_claims.reason: VT label only; not locally confirmed. Deepdive explicitly prohibits family attribution based on public labels alone.

not_supported_claims.claim: The sample performs network activity, C2 communication, or exfiltration.
not_supported_claims.reason: Not locally observed; the sample never reached its entry point. Public sandbox reports describe C2 behavior but this is external-only evidence.

not_supported_claims.claim: The sample establishes persistence, modifies the registry, or drops files.
not_supported_claims.reason: Not locally observed. Public sandbox reports describe RunOnce persistence and file writes, but these are external-only and not locally confirmed.

not_supported_claims.claim: The sample performs process injection, credential theft, or ransomware behavior.
not_supported_claims.reason: Not locally observed. No evidence of any specific payload behavior was captured.

not_supported_claims.claim: The cryptnet imports are fabricated or garbage exports.
not_supported_claims.reason: Directly contradicted by live IAT reads showing cryptnet imports resolve to real cryptnet.dll addresses.

not_supported_claims.claim: The pre-entry termination is an intentional anti-debug or anti-VM check.
not_supported_claims.reason: Refined by dynamic analysis: the termination is caused by unresolvable import dependencies (DESK.cpl absent, DispatchMessageA NULL), not an intentional anti-analysis check.

not_supported_claims.claim: The PECompact2-packed second stage performs any specific behavior or belongs to any known malware family.
not_supported_claims.reason: Unpacking the PECompact2 layer is required first. The terminal capability is indeterminate.

classification.overall_assessment: The sample is a multi-layer packed malware with a validated malicious loader architecture. The outer stub decrypts a self-relocating shellcode that performs in-place process hollowing to execute a PECompact2-packed second stage. The terminal payload capability is indeterminate, but the loader chain is confirmed malicious. Family attribution is not supported by local evidence.

recommended_actions.action: Unpack the PECompact2 layer to reveal the terminal payload import surface and execution path.
recommended_actions.reason: This is the highest-value remaining target. The terminal capability — network activity, persistence, or other behavior — is behind the PECompact2 packing.

recommended_actions.action: Bypass the loader gate to reach the module entry point and observe the full execution chain. Options: supply a stub DESK.cpl that exports DisplaySaveSettings, or patch IAT resolution earlier in the loader process.
recommended_actions.reason: A bypass would enable live validation of the recovered loader, the fwprintf hook, and the PECompact2 stage execution.

recommended_actions.action: After a loader gate bypass, breakpoint at the hook installation code and record the redirected destination address and enable state.
recommended_actions.reason: The hook is present in the shellcode but its purpose and enable state are unconfirmed.

recommended_actions.target: Public C2 IP 112.121.178.189 and RunOnce persistence
recommended_actions.action: After unpacking the PECompact2 stage and/or bypassing the loader gate, monitor for network activity, registry writes, and file creation to confirm or deny the public sandbox behavior.
recommended_actions.reason: Public sandbox reports describe HTTP callback to 112.121.178.189, RunOnce persistence, and file writes. These are external-only leads until locally confirmed.

recommended_actions.action: Read the raw file's OFT entry for the DispatchMessageA import slot to determine whether it is a genuine USER32 import or an obfuscated/corrupted entry.
recommended_actions.reason: The NULL slot may be a genuine environment issue or an intentional obfuscation. Resolving this informs the bypass strategy.

limitations: The sample never reached its entry point in the local analysis environment; all runtime conclusions are limited to the loader phase.
The terminal payload of the PECompact2-packed second stage is indeterminate until a further unpack round.
No network, filesystem, registry, or process-behavior observations were possible (no post-entry execution).
The decrypted shellcode's runtime destination buffer is unknown (content-independent but relevant for layout).
The msvcrt!fwprintf hook's enable state and target are unconfirmed.
Public IOCs (C2 IP 112.121.178.189, RunOnce persistence, mutexes, file paths) are external-only and not locally confirmed.
The DESK.cpl module is absent from the analysis VM, preventing import resolution bypass.
The recovered 1717-byte loader shellcode hash has no VirusTotal record (no public corroboration).
All static analysis of the shellcode and decoded PE is offline; no guest execution of the recovered artifacts occurred.
Family attribution is not supported by local evidence; VT labels are treated as unconfirmed context only.
